subject.title: Session files not being cleaned up (disk bloat)

question: Should OpenClaw add a proactive normal-maintenance sweep for stale session archive artifacts beyond the current deleted/reset retention helper and budget-triggered cleanup?
rationale: The implementation space crosses session retention policy: current main has partial temp and budget cleanup, while deleting retained archive files during startup or timers can affect users who expect those artifacts to remain until explicit cleanup or budget pressure.

options.title: Scope Broad Cleanup Policy
options.body: Define which stale `.deleted.*`, `.reset.*`, `.bak.*`, and temp artifacts should be removed during startup or periodic maintenance, and under which mode or retention setting.

options.title: Land Narrow Reporting Only
options.body: Treat https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/97103 as enough for now and leave proactive `.bak.*` and timer cleanup for later evidence.

options.title: Split By Artifact Class
options.body: Keep this issue as a parent while separate issues own deleted/reset reporting, temp cleanup, bak retention, and checkpoint or trajectory cleanup.

recommendation.title: Scope Broad Cleanup Policy
recommendation.body: Define which stale `.deleted.*`, `.reset.*`, `.bak.*`, and temp artifacts should be removed during startup or periodic maintenance, and under which mode or retention setting.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the session cleanup UX and maintenance controls that define the operator-facing cleanup policy.
